title: Normalized rational unit retraction for radicial-etale covers
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $A_{E,T}=p_T^*C(-,E)$ and $A_{\mathcal O_E,T}=p_T^*C(-,\mathcal O_E)$, with continuous-map condensed rings and their norm topologies [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $\Dbc(T,A_E)$ for bounded complexes with finite constant local models on finite constructible stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free, including rank zero [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $S$ be a scheme as above and let $f:W\to S$ factor as
$$W\xrightarrow{u}T\xrightarrow{e}S,$$
where $u$ is a finite universal homeomorphism and $e$ a finite etale surjection of constant degree $d\geq1$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-universal-homeomorphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. For every internal $A_{E,S}$-module $M$, not necessarily lisse, the functors $u_*,e_*,f_*$ on these coefficient modules are exact. The unit for $u^*\dashv u_*$ identifies $u_*u^*e^*M$ with $e^*M$. Under this identification there is an $A_{E,S}$-linear natural trace
$$t_M:f_*f^*M\longrightarrow M$$
characterized on an etale local splitting of $e$ into $d$ sheets by the sum of the $d$ copies of $M$. On the same splitting the unit $\eta_M:M\to f_*f^*M$ is the diagonal, and
$$t_M\eta_M=d\,1_M.$$
In the ordinary derived category the canonical comparison identifies $Rf_*(f^*M[0])$ with $(f_*f^*M)[0]$, and $\eta_M[0]$ is the derived adjunction unit under this identification. Consequently $(1/d)t_M[0]$ retracts that unit, so $M[0]$ is a retract of $Rf_*(f^*M[0])$. The scalar $1/d$ belongs to $E$, even if $\ell$ divides $d$. For a purely inseparable factor ($d=1$) the construction is the inverse to the universal-homeomorphism unit, rather than a field trace.

source.place: Agent continuous-coefficient extension of Tag 03SE (definition-trace-map), sum and degree formulas; proetale.tex Tag 09AB (lemma-thickening) for the radicial factor; original item step 6.

proof.text: Write $R_X=A_{E,X}$. The cartesian-coefficient theorem identifies module inverse image with the lift of the underlying inverse image, and the module pushforward definition gives its underlying direct image. Apply pro-etale topological invariance to $u$: its actual set-sheaf unit and counit are invertible. They remain invertible for abelian sheaves, since their inverses preserve addition by naturality. The module adjunction is the lifted adjunction: its unit and counit have these same underlying maps. The inverse of a bijective linear map is linear (apply the map to the two sides of the linearity equation), so these are module isomorphisms. Thus $u^*$ and $u_*$ are inverse equivalences, and $u_*$ is exact because an additive equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties. In particular put $N=e^*M$ to obtain the canonical identification $u_*u^*N\cong N$, inverse to the actual unit. This proves the radicial assertion for arbitrary modules, not only for finite local models.

source.place: Tag 09AB, lemma-thickening; the lift to module actions is written out using the cartesian coefficient and transport nodes

proof.text: Choose an etale covering family $q_i:U_i\to S$ splitting $e$, using the finite-etale local splitting lemma at each point; constant degree makes every nonempty splitting have $d$ sheets. The cited comparison makes etale maps weakly etale. These etale covering families are pro-etale coverings: over an affine test scheme, their open images cover, and quasi-compactness selects finitely many affine source opens covering it. Identify the pro-etale site of $U_i$ with the slice over $U_i$. On sheaves of rings the object-inverse-image comparison identifies inverse image with restriction; the cartesian coefficient isomorphism therefore identifies $R_{U_i}$ with $R_S|_{U_i}$. The same identification for modules follows from $R_{U_i}\otimes_{q_i^{-1}R_S}q_i^{-1}M\cong q_i^{-1}M$. We may work with sectionwise ring-module sheaves via the internal-module equivalence. Restriction of modules to each slice is exact by the cited ringed-site restriction theorem. Moreover these restrictions jointly detect zero objects: if $H|_{U_i}=0$, a section of $H$ on any $V$ vanishes on the covering $V\times_SU_i$, hence vanishes by the sheaf axiom. Exactness is consequently detected by these restrictions, since they preserve kernels and cokernels.

source.place: Tag 04HN, lemma-finite-etale-etale-local; pro-etale localization as in the cited localization nodes, with exact module restriction

proof.text: For any $R_T$-module $H$ and an object $V\to U_i$, the direct-image definition gives $(e_*H)(V)=H(V\times_ST)$. The chosen splitting writes $V\times_ST=\coprod_{j=1}^d V_j$ with each $V_j\cong V$. The sheaf axiom for this finite disjoint covering gives $H(\coprod_jV_j)\cong\prod_jH(V_j)$: intersections of distinct sheets are empty and a sheaf of modules has zero sections on the empty scheme. These restriction maps commute with all restrictions and with the $R_S(V)$-action. Thus $(e_*H)|_{U_i}\cong\prod_j s_{ij}^*H$, where $s_{ij}:U_i\to T$ are the sheets. Each sheet pullback is exact by cartesian coefficients. A finite product in an abelian category is a biproduct and preserves exact sequences: the direct-sum functor is left adjoint to the diagonal, hence preserves cokernels, while the product functor is right adjoint to the diagonal, hence preserves kernels. By the detection argument in step 2, $e_*$ is exact. Composition of module pushforwards gives $f_*\cong e_*u_*$, so $f_*$ is exact too. This finite-product calculation uses no exactness of infinite products.

source.place: Tag 03SE, definition-trace-map and following sheet description; finite disjoint-cover sheaf calculation and finite-biproduct exactness supplied explicitly

proof.text: Apply the preceding formula to $H=e^*M$. On each sheet the inverse-image restriction is canonically $M|_{U_i}$, so $(e_*e^*M)|_{U_i}\cong(M|_{U_i})^d$. Define $t_i$ to be the sum of its $d$ coordinates. These maps are linear and natural in $M$. To check compatibility of two splittings, intersect each sheet of one with each sheet of the other over $U_i\times_SU_h$. Their images are open and closed and cover the overlap. Refining by these intersections gives pieces on which the two labellings differ by a permutation: each sheet of either splitting meets exactly its matching sheet at every point. Finite sums are unchanged by this permutation. Thus the $t_i$ agree on a cover of the overlap, and agree everywhere by the separated sheaf axiom. For a section on an arbitrary $V$, apply the $t_i$ after restriction to $V\times_SU_i$ and glue their images in $M$; uniqueness makes this compatible with restriction, addition and scalar multiplication. This constructs the unique natural linear $t^e_M:e_*e^*M\to M$ with the stated local formula. No finite-rank or discreteness assumption on $M$ is involved.

source.place: Tag 03SE, definition-trace-map, characterization by localization and sum; permutation and gluing argument supplied for continuous module sheaves

proof.text: Use the composition isomorphisms to write $f_*f^*M\cong e_*u_*u^*e^*M$, and follow by $e_*$ of the inverse universal-homeomorphism unit from step 1. Denote the resulting isomorphism to $e_*e^*M$ by $c_M$, and set $t_M=t^e_Mc_M$. The unit of the composite adjunction is $M\xrightarrow{\eta^e_M}e_*e^*M\xrightarrow{e_*\eta^u_{e^*M}}e_*u_*u^*e^*M$; hence $c_M\eta^f_M=\eta^e_M$. In the split product description this latter unit sends a section $m$ to its restrictions on the $d$ sheets, namely $(m,\ldots,m)$ under the sheet identifications. Therefore $t_M\eta^f_M=\sum_{j=1}^dm=d\,1_M$, locally and hence globally. The isomorphisms used in $c_M$ are natural and linear, which proves those properties for $t_M$.

source.place: Tag 03SE, degree formula after definition-trace-map; composite-adjunction unit formula expanded explicitly

proof.text: Since $E$ contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$, its characteristic is zero. The positive integer $d$ is nonzero in $E$, so $1/d\in E$, irrespective of whether $\ell$ divides $d$. Constant scalar multiplication by $1/d$ is an endomorphism of the continuous coefficient sheaf: multiplication by a fixed field element is continuous, and the same holds after pullback from the point. Therefore $r_M=(1/d)t_M$ is a module morphism and $r_M\eta^f_M=(1/d)d\,1_M=1_M$. This uses no claim that $d$ is a unit in $\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: Tag 03SE, normalization when degree multiplication is invertible; scalar calculation for the specified field coefficients

proof.text: The cartesian-coefficient theorem makes $f^*$ exact, and step 3 makes $f_*$ exact. For these exact functors the total derived functors are canonically their termwise functors. In particular $Lf^*(M[0])\cong f^*M[0]$ and $Rf_*(f^*M[0])\cong(f_*f^*M)[0]$. Apply adjunction localization to the degreewise adjunction with its exact-functor comparison isomorphisms. Its explicit unit formula says that the derived unit on $M[0]$, after these comparisons, is the image of the ordinary unit $\eta^f_M[0]$. These are the canonical derived comparisons of the stipulated module derived pushpull, not an unrelated adjunction chosen on isomorphic functors. Equivalently, for a K-injective resolution $f^*M[0]\to I$, the unit is represented by $M[0]\to f_*f^*M[0]\to f_*I$; exactness makes the second arrow a quasi-isomorphism, giving exactly this identification.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; localized adjunction with unit formula as in lem-sfb-adjunction-localization

proof.text: Put the retraction $r_M$ of step 6 in degree zero and compose with the canonical comparison in step 7. Its composite with the derived unit is $(r_M\eta^f_M)[0]=1_{M[0]}$. This proves the claimed retract in the ordinary unbounded derived category. When $d=1$, the finite etale splitting has one sheet, $t^e$ and its unit are inverse, and $t_M$ is precisely the inverse universal-homeomorphism unit (with the degree-one etale identification). Thus even for a nontrivial purely inseparable field extension this is an inverse to a topos-equivalence unit; no algebraic field trace, which can vanish in characteristic $p$, was used. The zero module and the empty base give the same identities between zero maps.

Exactness of module restriction on a general ringed-site slice, with arbitrary ring sheaf; no purity assertion used.
Generic bridge from internal actions to sectionwise ring-module sheaves, preserving the underlying sections.
